q: Which four items make up the daily-teaching version of the scheme of work in Week 4?
o: Timeline and objectives, core tasks and skills, resources and technology, assessment methods
Theme, textbook, homework and mock exam
why: The four columns are Timeline and objectives, Core tasks and skills, Resources and technology, and Assessment methods.

q: A teacher writes the objective 'To do Exercise 3'. What is the main weakness?
o: It says what the page is, not what students will be able to do
why: A good objective says what students can do, using a verb you can see or hear.

q: What does the 'golden thread' link?
o: Syllabus aim, module target, lesson objective, task and check
The three papers and their marks
The teacher, the head and the parents
The starter, the plenary and the homework
why: Each lesson should connect back to a syllabus aim and forward to a check.

q: A scheme row says 'projector, audio file, speaker'. Which column is it in and what should be added?
o: Resources and technology, with a low-tech backup
Assessment methods, with a mark scheme
Core tasks and skills, with a timer
why: Technology can fail, so every digital resource needs a low-tech backup.

q: In a 55 minute lesson, which plan is most balanced?
o: Starter 6, input 10, guided practice 12, free production 15, plenary 8, close 2
why: A balanced lesson has a short starter, three main phases and a plenary.

q: A lesson is running late. What should the teacher do?
o: Shorten earlier phases or cut a task but keep the plenary
Skip the plenary and give all remaining tasks as homework
Speak faster and add more tasks
Keep going until the end of the book unit
why: The plenary shows what students learned, so it should not be cut.

q: What is the purpose of guided practice?
o: Students use new language with support in controlled tasks
Students speak freely without any help
The teacher reads the text aloud
why: Guided practice gives support before free production.

q: Which instruction check is best after explaining a pair task?
why: A specific question shows whether students know what to do.

q: Which activity is best as a starter?
o: Students put a jumbled sentence in order in pairs
The teacher explains a new grammar rule for ten minutes
Students copy the objective from the board
Students silently read a long text
why: A good starter is short, active, uses English and needs little preparation.

q: After exit tickets, what should a teacher do?
o: Sort them into got it, nearly and not yet, and plan the next lesson
Give them back the next term
why: Checks are useful only when the teacher acts on them.

q: Which pattern of vocabulary review works best?
o: Review after one day, one week and one month
Teach twenty words once and test at the end of the year
Review only words students ask about
why: Spaced review helps words move into long-term memory.

q: What is the correct order in the skills chain?
why: Students first take in language, notice it, practise it and then produce it.

q: A teacher uses the living stone plants article for reading, then a pair task giving advice, then an email. What pattern is this?
o: Reading, speaking and writing around one language pattern
why: One text supports several skills when you choose a pattern to notice.

q: Why is the final output task important in an integrated sequence?
o: Students need to use the language, not only recognise it
It is the only exam skill
why: Without output, students recognise but cannot use the language.

q: When should full timed past papers mainly be used?
o: At the end of modules, in mocks and in the final term
Every week from the first day
why: Use earlier stages to learn tasks and skills before timing full papers.

q: After students do a past paper, what is the most useful next step?
o: Mark with the mark scheme, find errors and redo
Move on to a new topic
Put the scripts in a file
why: Review and redo turns practice into learning.

q: How many marks and questions does the 2024 specimen Paper 1 have?
why: The specimen paper has 17 questions and 60 marks.

q: In the specimen mark scheme, what does Question 6 ask for?
o: Any three of four advice details about growing living stone plants
why: Question 6 is worth three marks for three advice details.

q: In specimen Exercise 3, how many marks are given for disadvantages and for reasons for popularity?
why: Question 8 gives three marks and Question 9 gives four marks.

q: In specimen Question 17, students write a report and must also do what?
o: Use some of the comment ideas and some ideas of their own
why: Content marks depend on developing ideas, not copying.

q: Why did students lose a mark for 'charging drivers' in a notes answer?
o: It was incomplete; it needed 'to enter parts of the city'
It was in the wrong order
why: Notes must carry the key meaning from the text.

q: In Exercise 2, the key word 'suggests' tells the student to look for what?
o: Implied meaning, not only a fact
why: The examiner report says implied meaning was hard for many students.

q: A student writes 'I really wanted to take place in the event.' What is the error?
why: The examiner report lists this common confusion.

q: For Paper 3, the examiner report says many centres marked pronunciation in what way?
o: Not as a stand-alone criterion, matching it to other marks
why: Pronunciation must be marked on its own evidence.

q: Which activity is an information gap?
o: Student A has the morning timetable and Student B the afternoon; they ask each other to complete it
Students fill gaps with one verb
why: Each student has information the other needs.

q: When is delayed correction best?
o: During a fluency discussion, with errors reviewed afterwards
why: Interrupting a fluency task can stop communication.

q: What is the best way to increase Student Talking Time in a class of 40?
o: One student speaks at a time
why: Pair work gives many students speaking time at once.

q: A teacher says 'CLT means no grammar'. What is the best reply?
o: Grammar is taught, but through use in communicative tasks
why: CLT teaches grammar in context.

q: What are the three stages of the Willis framework?
o: Pre-task, task cycle and language focus
why: Willis's 1996 framework has these three stages.

q: In TBL, when does the main focus on language form take place?
o: After the task, in the language focus
why: Students use language first and then study it.

q: What are the three parts of the task cycle?
why: Students do the task, plan their report and report to the class.

q: Which is the best reason to use PPP for conditionals and TBL for fluency?
o: PPP gives a clear structure for specific grammar, and TBL builds fluency
why: A good teacher uses both for different purposes.

q: What is the correct timing for Paper 3 Part 2?
o: 3 to 4 minutes including 1 minute of preparation
why: Students prepare for one minute and talk for up to two minutes.

q: What pattern do the three Part 1 questions follow?
o: Present or habits, a past story, an opinion or future
why: The teacher's notes show this pattern.

q: What do weaker Part 2 talks often do, according to the examiner report?
o: Talk about only one option or not state a preference
why: Students should cover both options and state a preference.

q: What should the examiner do if a candidate does not start speaking after 15 seconds in Part 2?
o: Read the prompt: Are you ready to start talking about the points on the card?
why: The notes give exact prompts.

q: What should the answer key for Exercise 1 style short answers show?
o: The correct answer and acceptable alternatives, with brackets for words not needed
why: This matches the style of the Cambridge mark scheme.

q: Which statement about a multiple-choice distractor is true?
o: It should be mentioned in the text but not answer the question
It should never appear in the text
It should be 'all of the above'
why: Good distractors are tempting because they use text words.

q: Which task is a good Part 2 card?
o: Two realistic options and a request to compare and say which you prefer and why
One option and a yes or no question
A long text to read aloud
why: It copies the Cambridge pattern.

q: Which statement about endorsed textbooks is correct?
o: They match the syllabus but do not replace it or fit every class
They are written by Cambridge examiners for each class
why: Endorsement is a check of fit, not a replacement.

q: What is scaffolding?
o: Temporary support that is removed as students improve
why: Scaffolds help students until they can work alone.

q: Which checklist item is student-friendly?
o: I answered all three bullet points
why: Use simple 'I' statements.

q: What must follow a self-assessment checklist?
o: One change or target to improve the work
why: Checking is useful only when it leads to action.

q: Which is a good first step when teaching students to use a checklist?
o: Model it on a sample answer, thinking aloud
Give it out with no instructions
why: Students need to see how it works first.

q: Which action best fits a 90-day plan for a teacher?
o: Teach three lessons from the new plan, start a tracker and review with a colleague
Change the whole course at once
why: Small steps, tracked and shared, make lasting change.
